It also omits chassis-bay-to-drive identity, empty-bay handling, BMC/NVMe-MI source path, controller-composite versus component temperature semantics, complete thresholds, UI mapping and safe credential handling.

V3.1 further binds each occupied bay to drive serial/FRU, PCIe BDF and NVMe controller, distinguishes BMC/NVMe-MI telemetry from host SMART data, and requires the exact temperature field equivalence before corroboration.

original_test_intent: Verify every expected NVMe temperature sensor represented by `TEMP_NVME_1~16` is individually readable in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, correctly mapped to chassis bays 1 through 16 and their installed drives or defined empty state, with specification-compliant value, units, status and supported thresholds.
original_method: Build a population-aware sixteen-bay matrix, resolve each stable BMC sensor and its NVMe-MI/management source, bind occupied bays to physical slot, drive FRU/serial and host PCIe/NVMe identity, and compare complete passive raw/UI fields with per-bay/drive specifications under recorded load and airflow. Preserve logs, drives and storage state.
manual_activity: The platform owner supplies the physical bay/backplane/PCIe/NVMe mapping, per-bay population and the BMC telemetry field used for each supported drive. Automation can collect all expected BMC records, inventory and UI rows; a human resolves bay/field/empty-state ambiguity and owns the verdict. No drive removal, I/O workload, reset or format is authorized.
required_inputs: Exact chassis/backplane/BMC/BIOS and NVMe bay 1-16 map to backplane port, PCIe root port/BDF, NVMe controller/namespace and installed drive PN/serial/FRU/firmware
Per-bay populated, empty, disabled and unavailable expectations, including whether a record remains when no drive is fitted
BMC management source for each reading, including controller/bus/mux/address and NVMe-MI/SMBus or vendor field, plus its mapping to controller composite or another temperature sensor
Stable SDR name/number/type/entity/instance and Dashboard/Server Health row for each expected bay
Drive-model and platform units, scaling/rounding, tolerance, threshold capability/values/hysteresis, health, freshness and update-lag specifications
Recorded drive power/workload, system load, fan/airflow state and any approved host `nvme smart-log` field equivalence
Validated ipmitool/API/browser versions, protected authentication and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or manual method
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, kernel or storage logs; NVMe, PCIe, media and thermal history is relevant evidence and must be preserved.

Do not issue `sensor get 'TEMP_NVME_1~16'` unless the vendor documents that literal record. Enumerate and query every expected bay sensor separately; one result or truncated inventory cannot represent sixteen bays.
Do not map BMC index to OS `nvmeX` numbering. Join physical bay/backplane port to drive serial/FRU and PCIe BDF/controller because host enumeration can change across boots.

Treat NVMe-MI/SMBus/I2C/I3C as BMC/platform-management scope by default. Require the controller/bus/mux/address and exact temperature field; a host SMART value alone does not prove the BMC target or field.

Do not remove/reseat or power-cycle a drive, reset a controller, generate I/O/thermal stress, change thresholds, format/write data or touch namespaces. This is passive telemetry validation, not storage functional or hot-swap testing.

Apply per-bay population rules, redact sensitive serials in user-facing evidence, avoid `-P`/assumed cipher 17 and unavailable Script execution, and stop without automatic retry on missing/duplicate/swapped bays, stale readings or BMC/UI/host disagreement.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, sixteen-bay/backplane/drive topology, BMC management path, client and Script; build a population-aware expected matrix before selecting records.
Capture each expected bay's complete BMC raw/API identity, value, units, supported thresholds, status and timestamp plus separate unchanged Dashboard and Server Health rows.
Bind occupied records to serial/FRU and BDF/controller and, only with approved field equivalence, compare time-aligned read-only host NVMe telemetry under the recorded workload/power/airflow state.

Report empty/disabled/unavailable, missing, duplicate, swapped, stale and divergent bays independently; preserve redacted evidence and perform no clear, I/O, hot-swap, reset, write, retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the bay/backplane/PCIe/NVMe/drive identity matrix and the expected record state for every populated or empty bay.
Define the BMC NVMe-MI/vendor source and temperature-field semantics, per-drive thresholds/tolerance/freshness and any host SMART equivalence, and approve the tool/Script.
Review all sixteen bay outcomes independently and issue the formal verdict without using one drive, a partial list or host enumeration as coverage for another bay.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as written because tilde shorthand is not an IPMI wildcard and one sensor response cannot prove sixteen bay records. The truncated fallback may omit sensors, and the command lacks bay/serial/BDF/source/UI/spec correlation, exposes credentials and assumes cipher support.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Enumerate complete BMC sensor and NVMe inventory, resolve every vendor-supported bay sensor ID, retrieve each through protected read-only access and correlate a sixteen-row UI/BMC/physical-bay/drive-identity matrix; use host telemetry only after exact field equivalence is approved.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: TEMP_NVME_1~16, Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading, readability/specification Criteria, generic clear text, Script URL, DeepSeek commands and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review expands the range without editing Master or performing drive/I/O actions.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a population-aware sixteen-row matrix keyed by physical bay and drive serial/FRU, document the BMC NVMe-MI/vendor telemetry path and exact temperature field, then compare complete raw/API and UI records with per-model limits and optional time-aligned equivalent host telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The exact chassis/backplane/NVMe population and BMC/SDR/WebUI build documented by the Project.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/backplane, BIOS/BMC/SDR/WebUI, every drive PN/serial/firmware, NVMe driver/tool, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Chassis/backplane bay topology, BMC NVMe-MI/SMBus sensor map, drive thermal specifications, SDR definitions, WebUI schema and Project configuration specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves a range into sixteen physical identity-bound records, adds management-path/field semantics and population-aware acceptance while preserving passive display coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Passive BMC temperatures do not validate storage I/O, media health, drive hot-swap, reset, workload thermal response, throttling, alarms or protection. Host composite temperature is not automatically the same BMC field.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Bay/backplane/drive map, BMC telemetry path/field, per-model acceptance and empty-state rules, workload/airflow/timing context, protected tool or reviewed Script and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Host NVMe numbering is unstable; mixed drive models have different sensors/limits; empty bays can omit records; BMC polling and UI rounding introduce lag; serials require redaction.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish/OEM or host NVMe telemetry as an approved alternate/corroboration only while preserving the original ipmitool method, recording interface/version/field and reason, obtaining engineer approval and proving equivalent per-bay identity, value, threshold, status and freshness coverage. A partial drive list, namespace identity or unmatched composite temperature is not equivalent to sixteen BMC bay sensors.
expected_evidence: Chassis/backplane/BMC/BIOS identity and sixteen-row physical bay-to-port/BDF/controller/namespace/drive PN-serial-FRU-firmware population matrix
BMC NVMe-MI/SMBus/vendor controller-bus-mux-address and exact temperature-field mapping for each supported drive
Complete per-bay raw records with stable IDs, values, units, threshold capabilities/values, status and timestamps
Separate redacted Dashboard and Server Health evidence for every expected bay with empty/disabled/unavailable semantics
Per-drive Project/vendor specification plus recorded drive workload/power and fan/airflow state, tolerance/update-lag and any approved equivalent host-telemetry comparison

Explicit missing/duplicate/swapped/stale/divergent disposition, pinned Script/tool security evidence, no-clear/no-I/O/no-hot-swap/no-write/no-retry proof, final storage/BMC health and engineer-owned sixteen-bay verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The range is unsafe as a literal command but clearly denotes NVMe sensors 1 through 16, and Items, UI Procedure and Criteria align on passive display/specification validation. Exact bay population, management source and fields are Project readiness inputs, not conflicting test purposes.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on hybrid classification while adding BMC NVMe-MI management-path ownership, exact temperature-field equivalence and serial/BDF identity controls.

review_improvement: Prevents a failed range query, partial sensor list or unstable OS numbering from being presented as sixteen-bay coverage, and prevents unrelated host SMART data or service-impacting storage actions from replacing the BMC display check.
independent_technical_reasoning: NVMe thermal evidence is only meaningful when a BMC sensor is joined to a physical bay and immutable drive identity; `nvmeX` numbering is not stable. BMC may obtain a composite temperature through NVMe-MI/SMBus while host SMART exposes multiple fields, so equivalence must be defined rather than assumed. Empty bays and mixed models also require per-row acceptance, and the source authorizes no I/O or drive manipulation.
